results.reason: This cell is DRIVABLE. The driver now runs Claude Desktop's command popup, /goal is in it, and three runs on 2026-09-07 each typed the command, accepted it, typed the goal text and submitted it — the agent ran a turn every time. What blocked all three was the RIG, not the recipe: the run itself started Claude Desktop, so the app inherited the driving Claude Code session's environment (CLAUDECODE=1, CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT, TERM_PROGRAM=vscode). Claude Code inherits it again from Desktop, and Irrlicht attributes the session to a terminal. Queried from the run's own daemon while it was in flight: launcher={"term_program":"vscode"}, host_bundle_id=null. The driver refuses a session it cannot attribute to Claude Desktop, which is the correct refusal — loosening it would let a run adopt a session it does not own. Sibling cell 2-12 recorded successfully the same evening against an earlier Claude Desktop process the rig had not started. Quit Claude Desktop, relaunch it through LaunchServices, and this cell is expected to record; the check and the commands are in desktop-evidence/launcher-attribution.md. The cell stays valid for cli-local, where it is recorded today.
